proved_scope: Finite directed logical-port reference graph: joins are output-to-input; input-to-output transfer requires an actual retained FLOW bridge. Ports/arcs are proof coordinates, not required runtime allocations.
Same logical-port meeting or a single correctly oriented join meeting constructively yields a full eligible-output-to-reader witness.
Full witness and existence of a logical meeting are constructively equivalent as a relation, independent of a production search scheduler.
Complete generic adjacency/exhaustion plus absence of a meeting supports a negative answer.

For the proposed TWO typed physical frontiers, forward closure joins a real FLOW input then queues its output; backward closure joins a real FLOW output then queues its input. Either exhausted typed frontier with no oriented cross-frontier join rules out a full witness.
Without a real FLOW transfer, an input port is stuck; an output-to-input path can contain only its direct join. An overlap-only left/broad/right chain cannot invent a transfer.
A newly enabled inherited join can connect two already visited local frontier ports without any identical-port intersection or newly discovered state.
A positive finite example crosses one actual FLOW bridge between its two joins.
